steps.title: Clean the data
steps.detail: Dropped 2 duplicate rows and clipped 10 impossible negative Physical_Activity_Hours values to 0, leaving 4,998 rows.

steps.title: Define features & target
steps.detail: 12 inputs: 6 numeric, 1 ordinal (Stress_Level) and 5 nominal columns. All 111 countries are kept instead of collapsing to Top-10 + Other - this alone lifted accuracy noticeably.

steps.title: Split train / test
steps.detail: 70 / 30 split with random_state=42: 3,498 training rows and 1,500 untouched test rows, identical to the original notebook for a fair comparison.

steps.title: Build preprocessing pipelines
steps.detail: Linear model: impute + scale + encode. Tree models: impute + encode only, because trees are invariant to monotonic scaling. Everything lives inside a sklearn Pipeline so there is no train/test leakage.

steps.title: Train three models
steps.detail: Linear Regression (0.04s), Random Forest (25.3s) and Extra Trees (23.7s), each wrapped with its preprocessor.

steps.title: Evaluate on the test set
steps.detail: Compared R2, MAE and RMSE. Extra Trees reached R2 0.942 vs 0.912 (Random Forest) and 0.787 (Linear).

steps.title: Cross-validate
steps.detail: 5-fold CV on the training data confirms the ranking is not an artefact of one lucky split; fold-to-fold standard deviation stays tiny.

steps.title: Interpret & diagnose
steps.detail: Permutation importance on the test set shows which inputs the model truly depends on; residual histograms and actual-vs-predicted plots check for bias and heteroscedasticity.

steps.title: Select, refit & export
steps.detail: Extra Trees wins. The complete preprocessing + model pipeline is refit on all 4,998 rows and saved with joblib so the API can accept raw inputs.

linear_regression.name: Linear Regression
linear_regression.tagline: Fast, transparent baseline that assumes a straight-line relationship.
linear_regression.description: Fits one coefficient per (scaled / one-hot encoded) input. It is the benchmark every other model has to beat. Because it can only add up independent linear effects, it cannot capture interactions such as 'long usage hurts more when sleep is short'.
preprocessing: One-hot encoding for 5 nominal columns (incl. all 111 countries)
pros: Instantly trainable and easy to explain
cons: Cannot model non-linear effects or interactions

random_forest.name: Random Forest
random_forest.tagline: 300 decorrelated trees, each trained on a bootstrap sample, averaged together.
random_forest.description: Each tree sees a bootstrap sample and picks the best split among candidate features. Averaging many high-variance trees yields a stable, non-linear model that handles interactions automatically and needs no feature scaling.
preprocessing: Median imputation for numerics (no scaling needed for trees)
pros: Robust to outliers and unscaled data
cons: Slower and bigger than linear models
Searches for the *best* split, which can over-fit noise

extra_trees.name: Extra Trees
extra_trees.tagline: Like Random Forest, but split thresholds are drawn at random — more variance reduction.
extra_trees.description: Extremely Randomised Trees train on the full dataset (no bootstrap) and choose split thresholds at random instead of optimising them. That extra randomness acts as strong regularisation, which works very well on this smooth, low-noise target. This is the model deployed in the Predict page.
pros: Highest accuracy and lowest error here
Faster to train than Random Forest
cons: Needs full pipeline at inference time
Impurity importances are biased - permutation importance used instead
